feed.title: Medical Machine Learning Lab
feed.subtitle: Clinical decisions are made with incomplete, noisy, and heterogeneous data under uncertainty. At M2L Lab, we develop AI methods that support clinicians with reliable, interpretable, and scalable intelligence. Our research focuses on scalable and efficient learning across medical modalities, interpretability and reasoning, and robustness and human-centeredness, aiming for reliable and trustworthy AI in medicine.

entry.title: Deep Dive Session at AI Grid Summit

link.title: Deep Dive Session at AI Grid Summit

entry.content: At the AI Grid Summit 2026, I had the pleasure to talk about the topic of our newest preprint, “Hidden Data Challenges in Clinical Machine Learning”, in a deep dive session together with co-author Dennis Fast from TU Berlin. Using MIMIC-IV, we investigate how choices around timestamps, clinical endpoints, and missing data can affect data leakage, misalignment and what models actually learn.
